topic: Corrected terminal-row compatibility and the covariance information frontier for soft-intervention linear causal disentanglement. For every 2<=p<=q and q-node DAG G, observe one baseline and one unknown-target single-node soft-intervention context per latent node in X^(k)=F(I-Lambda^(k))^-1 epsilon^(k), with full-row-rank mixing, noncollinear columns, exact nonzero graph support, independent non-Gaussian errors, and algebraically independent nonzero incoming-edge changes. Define Hsoft(G) from the actual intervention rows h_k^T=delta_k^T(I-Lambda^0)^-1, not the published observational-path substitution, with exact support and noncancellation admissibility; define Cov_p(G) by generic positive-real covariance compatibility. Prove: (1) a sound-and-complete terminal-copy strict-gammoid plus affine-hyperplane certificate algorithm for Hsoft and an exact characterization of when the published Definition 3.14 class agrees; (2) Cov_q(G)=Hsoft(G) under square mixing by whitening and ancestor-order recovery, including all sign, scale, support, and variance branches; and (3) for p<q, a graph-specific non-QE positive-real projection-completeness criterion deciding Cov_p(G)\Hsoft(G), with generic realization or separator certificates, explicit complexity, and infinite equality and strict families. Credit Leyes Carreno--Meroni--Seigal 2025 Theorem 1.7, Definition 3.14, and Problems 5.1--5.2, and Squires et al. 2023 for injective soft-intervention transitive-closure recovery. The companion LCD workflow is a prospective same-question consumer: it must report the corrected compatible DAG set and whether high cumulants genuinely remove covariance alternatives. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: Exact symbolic checks give a generic four-node determinant gamma(beta*d-b*delta) refuting the observational-path substitution, five positive-definite square covariances, and a separate p=2 rational covariance collision with actual-row obstruction -2. Terminal-copy linkage and affine support testing, square covariance equality, an infinite small-component equality family, and a complete regular reduction of the four-node noninjective fork to eight two-scalar positive systems were derived. A stronger rational collision keeps candidate variances T+144/121 and 19/4 positive for every T>0, T!=1. Classical-linkage, generic-QE, degenerate-rank, all-sign/variance-chamber, rational-certificate, finite-sample, consumer-deployment, and bounded-literature failure modes were checked; the all-p positive chamber union remains open. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Prove a graph-specific, non-QE positive-real projection-completeness criterion deciding whether the finite union of every legal covariance branch has complement of empty relative interior in the full true parameter domain. EARLY KILL TEST: Complete the eight-branch two-scalar positive-feasibility classification of the four-node p=2 fork over its full true parameter domain and verify every proposed separator against the original context covariance equations; pivot if the structured reduction is unsound or generalizes only through unrestricted quantifier elimination. STRONGEST-FORM DRAFT (unverified, gaps listed inside): <repo-root>/internal/presolve_drafts/eid_softlcd_terminalrow_complete.md.

open_problems.open_problem: Determine whether Definition 3.14's observational-path rank conditions are equivalent to soft-intervention compatibility based on the actual changed mechanism rows, and otherwise replace them with a sound-and-complete terminal-copy linkage and affine-span criterion.

source_refs.claim: Definition 3.14 uses ranks of baseline inverse path matrices, while Problem 5.1 asks for a combinatorial description of the compatibility class.
source_refs.author: Paula Leyes Carreno, Chiara Meroni, Anna Seigal

source_refs.claim: Generic ranks of covariance submatrices have a complete graph-theoretic trek-separation characterization based on path-polynomial determinant expansions.
source_refs.author: Seth Sullivant, Kelli Talaska, Jan Draisma

source_refs.excerpt: Missing interventions, soft or multitarget interventions, latent coordinate mixing ... are outside the positive theorem.
sound-and-complete O(p^4) real-arithmetic membership certificate checking baseline factorization and every surgery

open_problems.why_unsolved: The published argument replaces entries containing changed-minus-baseline edge coefficients by baseline inverse-path expressions, but genericity alone does not prove that actual-row compatibility is invariant under this substitution. The closest prior CausalSmith construction certifies perfect observed-coordinate surgeries using coordinate-isolated precision differences and explicitly excludes soft interventions and latent mixing. Its first proof step fails here because the load-bearing object is h_k^T=delta_k^T(I-Lambda^0)^-1 after projection by F. A complete criterion must control terminal reuse, repeated path monomials, noncancellation, exact support, and whether the distinguished column lies in the affine span generated by the changed row's child columns.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A theorem giving an exact agreement condition or counterexample for Definition 3.14, followed by a polynomial-time strict-gammoid terminal-copy algorithm that accepts exactly the actual-row-compatible graph pairs and returns either a linkage certificate or an affine-hyperplane obstruction.

writing_exemplar.why: Its progression from a polynomial compatibility system to a rank-defined graph class and then to Problem 5.1 is the closest framing for a corrected characterization.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Soft interventions leave a positive-dimensional parameter fiber -> higher cumulants restrict compatible DAGs through rank conditions -> the published ranks substitute baseline path data for changed rows -> formulate and characterize compatibility using the actual intervention rows.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt path-sum determinant expansions and the cancellation proof for intersecting trek systems to convert generic row rank into a vertex-disjoint terminal linkage condition.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The corrected compatibility predicate is a generic rank and column-span question for entries of an inverse-DAG path matrix, matching the algebra-to-linkage structure of trek separation.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt the half-trek criterion's max-flow verification and constructive recovery proof, adding copied terminals and an affine-span test.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The requested resolution requires an efficient certificate-producing algorithm as well as a determinant identity.

open_problems.open_problem: For square full-row-rank mixing p=q, determine whether positive-real covariance compatibility equals corrected actual-row soft-intervention compatibility for every DAG and every admissible target-permutation, sign, scale, support, and variance branch.

source_refs.claim: Problem 5.2 asks whether the higher-cumulant compatible class is strictly contained in the covariance-compatible class.
source_refs.author: Paula Leyes Carreno, Chiara Meroni, Anna Seigal

source_refs.claim: With injective mixing, covariance and precision matrices from generic soft interventions recover the transitive closure; perfect interventions recover the DAG.
source_refs.author: Chandler Squires, Anna Seigal, Salil S. Bhate, Caroline Uhler

source_refs.excerpt: Theorem 1.6 gives higher-order-cumulant perfect-intervention recovery under a known observational context
It does not establish a real information-order lower bound, uniform finite-sample inference, or dependent-latent robustn

open_problems.why_unsolved: Leyes Carreno et al. leave covariance-versus-higher-cumulant graph containment open, while Squires et al. recover only the soft-intervention transitive closure from covariance under injective mixing rather than comparing the resulting compatible class with actual-row compatibility. The repository evidence likewise separates covariance-only recovery from higher-cumulant recovery without a common graph-specific information frontier. Although square mixing permits whitening, completeness still requires proving that every positive-real covariance factorization shares an ancestor order and that no alternative survives through target relabeling, row signs and scales, exact-support constraints, or positive error-variance chambers.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A constructive generic theorem proving Cov_q(G)=Hsoft(G) for every q-node DAG, with a whitening and ancestor-order inverse covering every discrete and positive-variance branch, or a smallest positive-real counterexample with a fully stated failure regime.

writing_exemplar.why: It directly frames the comparison between covariance-compatible and higher-cumulant-compatible graph classes.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Soft interventions identify only a graph class -> higher cumulants define a rank-refined class -> covariance may admit more alternatives -> determine whether invertible square mixing closes the information gap.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt whitening of context precision matrices, inductive recovery of rank-one directions, partial-order RQ decomposition, and Cholesky reconstruction while explicitly tracking every target, sign, and scale branch.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the existing covariance-only recovery argument in the injective linear-LCD regime; the missing step is upgrading transitive-closure recovery to equality with the corrected compatibility class.

open_problems.open_problem: For p<q, construct a graph-specific non-quantifier-elimination criterion deciding whether all legal positive-real covariance branches are generically projection-complete or whether Cov_p(G) contains a relatively open family of alternatives outside corrected Hsoft(G).

source_refs.claim: Problem 5.2 asks whether covariance compatibility is strictly larger, while Proposition 3.6 only establishes covariance parameter nonidentifiability for an overcomplete perfect-intervention example.
source_refs.author: Paula Leyes Carreno, Chiara Meroni, Anna Seigal

open_problems.why_unsolved: The published overcomplete negative result concerns parameter nonuniqueness for a special perfect-intervention model, not which distinct DAGs generically survive covariance under soft interventions. Projection through an unknown p-by-q mixing matrix produces a nonconvex semialgebraic image, and complex-algebraic solvability can rely on zero supported edges, cancellations, or nonpositive error variances. Prior CausalSmith work isolates punctured affine feasibility, Hall-Rado ranks, lower-dimensional chart incidences, and duplicate branch enumeration as the obstacles hidden by unrestricted real quantifier elimination. The first proof step that changes is the replacement of response-chart source partitions by terminal-copy linkages coupled to positive-definite covariance projection and exact sign, scale, support, and variance chambers.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A finite combinatorial-semialgebraic invariant, with explicit termination and bit-complexity bounds, that decides whether Cov_p(G)\Hsoft(G) has nonempty relative interior and returns either a generic positive-real realization or a valid linkage, affine, or positivity separator, together with infinite equality and strictness families.

writing_exemplar.why: Problem 5.2 and Proposition 3.6 give the cleanest motivation from overcomplete covariance nonidentifiability to a graph-level information frontier.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Overcomplete mixing destroys covariance parameter identification -> graph compatibility may nevertheless remain restricted -> positivity and shared-context structure determine which algebraic alternatives are real -> characterize the graph-specific covariance frontier.

method_exemplars.technique: Translate compatibility into a structured positive-semidefinite decomposition, prove a converse realization theorem, and derive incompatibility witnesses from dual separating hyperplanes.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The requested criterion likewise needs both positive-real realizations and explicit separators, although soft-intervention coupling makes its feasible set nonconvex.

method_exemplars.technique: Push parameter equations, strict inequalities, and inequations through rational inverse charts to retain exact semialgebraic model-membership conditions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired characterization must preserve variance positivity and nonvanishing support after projection, information lost by ordinary complex or Zariski implicitization.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt latent-factor half-trek systems that certify rational recovery through bounded graph searches instead of unstructured latent projection.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies a graph-specific covariance criterion for dense latent effects, structurally analogous to retaining the shared overcomplete mixing and intervention mechanisms here.

open_problems.open_problem: Classify, for every p≤q and candidate DAG pair (G,G'), the least cumulant order that generically excludes G' when covariance does not, or prove that G' survives every available cumulant order.

source_refs.claim: The Outlook states that higher-order cumulants can reduce parameter-space degree but leaves open whether they restrict the compatible DAG set.
source_refs.author: Paula Leyes Carreno, Chiara Meroni, Anna Seigal

source_refs.claim: Multi-trek separation characterizes graph-forced vanishing determinants in higher-order cumulant subtensors, including models with hidden variables.
source_refs.author: Elina Robeva, Jean-Baptiste Seby
source_refs.venue: SIAM Journal on Applied Algebra and Geometry

source_refs.claim: Overcomplete ICA admits an if-and-only-if mixing-identifiability characterization based on rank-one symmetric matrices in a linear space.
source_refs.author: Kexin Wang, Anna Seigal

open_problems.why_unsolved: A decrease in the degree or dimension of a coupled tensor-decomposition fiber does not imply that a candidate DAG disappears. Multi-trek separation characterizes individual cumulant-subtensor rank constraints, and overcomplete ICA characterizes recovery of independent mixing columns, but neither incorporates unknown intervention-target alignment, actual changed structural rows, and structural-equation coupling across every LCD context. Consequently, the companion workflow currently lacks a theorem-level way to distinguish a genuine cumulant removal of a covariance alternative from mere parameter refinement within the same compatible graph.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A graph-pair invariant d*(G,G') in {2,3,...,infinity} such that cumulants through order d* first separate G from G', accompanied by an explicit separating minor or coupled-factor invariant when d* is finite and a generic all-orders alternative realization when d*=infinity.

writing_exemplar.why: It poses the covariance-versus-higher-cumulant graph question and organizes the model by cumulant order.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Covariance leaves graph alternatives -> higher cumulants can shrink parameter fibers -> fiber shrinkage need not remove a graph -> identify the first cumulant order that truly separates each alternative.

method_exemplars.technique: Represent cumulant entries by multi-trek monomials and prove determinant vanishing through multi-trek separation.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A finite d*(G,G') certificate should be a graph-readable higher-order invariant that vanishes for one candidate and not the other.

method_exemplars.technique: Characterize mixing recovery through the rank-one locus of a linear space of symmetric matrices and convert that characterization into a recovery algorithm.
method_exemplars.why_closest: For p<q, using a separating cumulant first requires determining whether its overcomplete rank-one factors are uniquely recoverable.

method_exemplars.technique: Construct fourth-moment ICA estimators through FOBI, FastICA, and JADE estimating equations and derive root-n asymptotic normality with componentwise asymptotic variances.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Once a population fourth-cumulant invariant separates two graph classes, this is the closest established route to a sampling limit law, although context coupling and overcompleteness remain to be handled.

literature_map:
Leyes Carreno, Meroni, and Seigal (2025), Linear Causal Disentanglement via Higher-Order Cumulants, is the anchor: Theorem 1.7 defines a soft-intervention compatibility class, while Problems 5.1–5.2 leave its combinatorial description and covariance comparison open.
Squires, Seigal, Bhate, and Uhler (ICML 2023), Linear Causal Disentanglement via Interventions, proves covariance recovery of the transitive closure for generic soft interventions under injective mixing and full DAG recovery for perfect interventions.
The tension is exact: injective covariance identifies ancestor order, but the 2025 paper does not determine whether higher cumulants further shrink the compatible DAG set in the square case.
Zhang et al. (2023), Identifiability Guarantees for Causal Disentanglement from Soft Interventions, obtains equivalence-class recovery under generalized faithfulness for injective mixing but not overcomplete covariance compatibility.
Buchholz et al. (NeurIPS 2023), Learning Linear Causal Representations from Interventions under General Nonlinear Mixing, uses Gaussian precision differences; its soft-intervention guarantee stops at partial-order recovery.
Varici et al. (JMLR 2025), Score-based Causal Representation Learning, recovers ancestors under general soft interventions and the full graph under stronger mechanism restrictions.
von Kügelgen et al. (NeurIPS 2023), Nonparametric Identifiability of Causal Representations from Unknown Interventions, treats unknown perfect interventions rather than the soft covariance-versus-cumulant frontier.
Wang and Seigal (Bernoulli 2026), Identifiability of Overcomplete Independent Component Analysis, gives an exact rank-one-subspace criterion but has no shared causal-DAG or intervention-row constraints.
De Lathauwer, Castaing, and Cardoso (IEEE TSP 2007) supplies constructive overcomplete fourth-cumulant estimation machinery without a graph-compatibility theorem.
Kileel and Pereira (arXiv:1912.04007) and Kileel, Klock, and Pereira (arXiv:2110.15821) provide tensor-decomposition and noisy-landscape machinery relevant to empirical higher-cumulant recovery.
Sullivant, Talaska, and Draisma (Annals of Statistics 2010) gives a path/linkage characterization of generic covariance-submatrix rank; Robeva and Seby (SIAAG 2021) extends this logic to higher-order cumulants.
Foygel, Draisma, and Drton (Annals of Statistics 2012) and Foygel Barber et al. (Annals of Statistics 2022) show how trek criteria yield efficient generic-identifiability certificates, including latent-factor models.
Boege and Solus (arXiv:2410.23102) retains real inequalities under birational implicitization, while Kela et al. (IEEE TIT 2020) supplies positive-semidefinite compatibility realizations and dual separators.
The bounded search found no later paper correcting the actual-intervention-row substitution, proving square Cov_q equality, or giving a non-QE graph-specific positive-real projection criterion for p<q.
